name: Wyoming
status_why: The Secretary posts PDF summaries as each county finishes; slow, and not a data feed.
system: Secretary of State's own site (sos.wyo.gov, ASP.NET): PDF summaries updated through the night as each county finishes and the Secretary checks it; a results zip afterwards.

results_page.label: Wyoming Secretary of State: election results
results_page.source: answered one request with the kit's User-Agent (N4, 2026-10-10)

election.how_to_find: Poll for the general results page.

feeds.updates: updated through election night as a county reports 100 percent and the Secretary verifies it (2024 page wording); not precinct by precinct
feeds.note: PDF, not a data feed. Pages answered 200 on 2026-10-09.
The kit reads the 2026 primary zip.

local: Yes: the state page says county and local results are on the county clerks' sites. Laramie (laramiecountywy.gov Elections), Natrona (natronacounty-wy.gov), Campbell (campbellcountywy.gov/867/Elections), Park (parkcounty-wy.gov/county-elections). Not requested.
how_counted: The Secretary of State adds a county's results once the county has counted every ballot and the office has checked it.
vote_types: No (summaries carry totals, undervotes, overvotes, provisional ballots).

certify.rule: Meets no later than the second Wednesday after the election (Wyo. Stat. 22-16-118).
certify.local_rule: County boards by the first Friday after the election (22-16-103).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

condition: PDF summaries, a county at a time once the county is complete and checked.
scout_plan: Readable but slow and in PDF. Poll the general results page every ten minutes or so for new or changed summary PDFs, read them with ballot/pdftext.py, and show each county as 'all in' or 'not yet'. Local results only from county clerks after the night; leave them for after Nov 3.
sources: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself
